rai:dataCollectionRawData: All inputs are synthetic task descriptions; all environments are sandboxed; no human subjects or scraped data.
rai:dataAnnotation: Per-action and per-trajectory suspicion scores were annotated by automated LLM-based monitors (gpt-4.1-nano, Claude Haiku/Opus, etc.). No human annotation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. Task environments use synthetic users, fake credentials, and dummy data. TODO: confirm by manually inspecting a random sample of N trajectories.
rai:dataBiases: TODO: 10 environments are an intentionally narrow sample of Linux SaaS systems. Results may not generalize to (a) non-Linux systems, (b) production-scale infrastructure, (c) human-in-the-loop workflows, (d) closed-source enterprise software. See paper §6.
rai:dataLimitations: Trajectories use a fixed set of agent policies and monitor configurations from the date of collection — newer models may behave qualitatively differently. Action-level scores are LLM-generated and inherit model biases.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (1) evaluating AI control protocols, (2) developing new monitors, (3) developing new attack policies, (4) studying agent behavior patterns. Out-of-scope: claims about specific deployed AI systems' real-world safety.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Dual-use disclosure: this dataset contains examples of subtle sabotage strategies. Risk of misuse for developing real-world attacks is mitigated by (a) all attacks operate in sandboxed environments and target synthetic systems, (b) attack capabilities documented are within the publicly known capability frontier, (c) the dataset's primary value is to defenders developing detection methods.
